περίπλοος , ον, contr.
περιπλόκ-πλους , gen. πλου, nom. pl. -πλοι :—
A.circumnavigation, c. gen., “τὸν π. τοῦ Ἄθω”
Hdt. 6.95
; “περὶ Πελοπόννησον”
Th. 2.80
, cf. 8.4 ; “τὸν π. τὸν εἰς Κέρκυραν”
Aeschin. 3.243
; esp. round the enemy's fleet, X. HG 1.6.31 : metaph., of a journey by land, Call. Fr. 278 ; of the journey of the soul in transmigration,
Diog.Oen. 35 .
II. account of a coasting voyage (opp. περίοδος of a land-journey), “γράφειν τὸν π. τῆς ἔξω θαλάσσης”
Luc. Hist.Conscr. 31
: Periplus is the title of several geograph. works, still extant, by Scylax, Agatharchides, Arrian, etc.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
